messages:
ian: Quick sync — proposal to derive route-level SLOs from spans instead of only metrics. idea: canonicalize span->route, compute p95/p99 of server_processing (exclude downstream), keep counts for error budgets. who objects?
marie: +1 on canonicalization. main worry: span name variability from older SDKs. need a mapping step.
anjali: sampling will bite us here. what retention are we proposing for raw spans vs rollups?
ian: thinking raw spans 7d, aggregated rollups (per-route hourly/daily) kept 90d for SLO windows. raw longer for Dedicated customers.
liu: 7d raw seems low for long-tail investigations. can we do differential retention: high-error routes keep raw 30d, others 7d?
samir: that makes sense. we can mark routes that exceed error budget and bump sampling/retention automatically.
sre-ops: alerting tie-in: if route exceeds error budget, escalate and auto-increase full-trace sampling to 1000rpm for 30m. but that impacts billing.
marie: need to be explicit about quotas — increased sampling should not silently blow customer quotas. UI prompt + confirmation? :warning:
ian: agree. UX: when a route enters investigation mode, console shows "Increase trace capture for 30m" with estimated cost delta.
anjali: can we show cost delta? we already estimate token costs; trace sampling cost calc should be doable.
liu: for canonicalization, propose a config file: route_map = {"/v1/generate":"generate.handler", "chat.start":"chat.handler"} — apply at ingest. fall back to span attributes (http.route, rpc.method).
samir: +1. also add a hashing of dynamic path segments so /users/123 -> /users/:id before grouping.
ian: code snippet for TraceQL query we'd run for SLO:```traceql
from spans
where route = "generate.handler"
aggregate p99(server_processing_ms) by time(5m)
```
marie: visual: latency breakdown waterfall per-route — queueing | scheduling | model_inference | downstream_io. we should surface model time separately to help routing policy decisions (eg fallback to cheaper variant).
sre-ops: agree. telemetry pipeline needs to produce those breakdown fields at ingest: queue_ms, sched_ms, inference_ms, downstream_ms. otherwise UI has to approximate.
anjali: how expensive is computing p99 on raw spans in near-real-time? can we rely on streaming approximate algorithms (T-Digest) on rollups?
liu: yes, TDigest for rollups. raw trace store can be sampled. rollup pipeline emits tdigest per-route per-5m window, stored as metric series for alerts.
samir: decision point: do we store tdigest blobs in TSDB or as precomputed quantiles? storing tdigest lets us requery quantiles for different windows. cost tradeoff.
ian: prefer tdigest blobs in long-term object store but push precomputed p50/p95/p99 to metrics for fast dashboard/alerts.
marie: can we derive error budget from trace-derived latency SLOs? e.g., consider any trace with server_processing > p99_threshold as 'bad' and compute burn_rate from that.
sre-ops: yes. implement: error_count = count(spans where server_processing_ms > SLO_ms). burn_rate = error_count / total_requests over window. tie to incident rules.
anjali: tagging: we must ensure route attribution is stable across rollouts. when model variant A->B rollout, route stays same but inference_ms distribution will change — rollouts UX should let product compare pre/post p95 with diff test.
ian: rollout UX: allow canary window that overlays trace-derived tdigests for canary vs baseline, with automatic significance test.
sre-ops: from ops side, also enforce retention policy per-tenant. Dedicated customers may opt-in to 90d raw retention with surcharge.
samir: quick OTEL exporter config idea for sampling policy (example):```yaml
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [redwood-otlp]
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: error_rate_high
        decision: keep_if(error.status_code >= 500)
```
liu: tail sampling is good; also use adaptive head-based + tail to keep latency-sensitive microbursts.
marie: UX question: how do we present SLOs computed from traces vs metrics? users might be confused if they differ. we should show a small explainer and a mapping table.
ian: yes, dashboard panel: "metric SLO vs trace SLO" with note about method differences and sampling. default alerts still use metric SLO but customers can opt-in to trace-SLO alerts.
anjali: next steps?
ian: I'll draft an RFC: sections: canonicalization rules, sampling & retention policy, rollup pipeline (tdigest), UI mockups for canary & cost estimate, alerting integration. action items: @marie mockups, @liu retention cost model, @samir sampling automation. I'll open a PR by EOD.
deploy-bot: telemetry/config v2 pushed to staging: https://ci.internal/redwood/telemetry/5678 :rocket:
ian: thanks — we'll iterate on the RFC and link to the staging config for examples.
